summary: Phase A/B/C testing for Webstore Owner Connect + Founders-only tier hiding. Created /app/backend/tests/test_iteration140_owner_connect_endpoints.py with 21 tests covering fee-preview math, tenant invite endpoints (quick + portal), public token-bound onboarding endpoints, portal signup + auth, and the webstore activation gate. 18/21 passed. The 3 failures are all caused by a single root-cause backend bug (UserRole enum missing 'webstore_owner'). The existing test_fees_and_owner_connect.py still passes 10/10. Frontend Phase B (tier hiding) and Phase C (owner-portal pages) UI verified visually.

critical.issue: All authenticated owner-portal endpoints return 500 Internal Server Error. Root cause: models/enums.py UserRole enum only allows ('owner','admin','staff','platform_admin') — does NOT include 'webstore_owner'. routes/webstore_owners.py portal_signup creates users with role='webstore_owner', but when those users authenticate via get_current_active_user, Pydantic UserInDB validation fails. Backend log: "pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for UserInDB. Input should be 'owner', 'admin', 'staff' or 'platform_admin' [type=enum, input_value='webstore_owner']". This breaks the ENTIRE Owner Portal authenticated flow (Phase C signup→login→dashboard).

integration_issues.issue: Even after fix lands on backend, the /owner-portal dashboard will fail to call /api/owner-portal/me until the UserRole enum is updated. UI itself renders the login form correctly on dark theme.

action_items: CRITICAL: Add WEBSTORE_OWNER = 'webstore_owner' to UserRole enum in /app/backend/models/enums.py so the new role passes UserInDB Pydantic validation. After fix, re-run test_iteration140_owner_connect_endpoints.py — the remaining 3 tests should pass without further changes.

Optional: consider also adding webstore_owner to ROLE_PERMISSIONS in models/auth.py with an empty/whitelist permission set so RBAC checks don't crash if any code path inspects permissions for this role.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/webstore_owners.py imports get_password_hash, create_access_token from server module at call-time inside portal_signup — works, but creates an implicit cyclic-import risk. Consider importing from a dedicated auth/security module.

stripe_service.calculate_platform_fee_cents has a 1-cent micro-payment floor that drops below the advertised 2.2%+$0.20 for tiny amounts (e.g. $0.05 invoice clamps to 4c). Confirmed by test_micro_payment_floor — acceptable but worth a note in the landing-page small print.
webstore_owner_invites collection has no TTL index — expired invites are detected at fetch but never cleaned up. Recommend a Mongo TTL index on expires_at to prevent unbounded growth.
_resolve_invite returns 404 for unknown tokens but the requirement says expired/unknown → 410/404 — current behavior matches (410 for known-but-expired, 404 for unknown). Good.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on smoke checks executed (login page, invalid-token landings, /pricing-legacy redirect, /pricing-plans Founders-only)

seed_data_creation: Test webstore (TEST_OwnerConnect_*) + two owner_invites + one webstore_owner user (TEST_portal_*@example.com). All cleaned up by fixture teardown + teardown_module(). Verified no TEST_ records remain in mongo after the run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: After main agent adds WEBSTORE_OWNER to UserRole enum, simply rerun: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_iteration140_owner_connect_endpoints.py -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/iteration140_results.xml. Expect 21/21. Phase A fee math + Phase B tier hiding + public Phase C onboard pages already verified end-to-end; the gap is solely the authenticated owner-portal path which fails at the UserInDB schema layer.
rca_of_the_issue: TEST_PORTAL_OWNER_500: Pydantic UserInDB model strictly types `role: UserRole` where UserRole = Enum('owner','admin','staff','platform_admin'). When routes/webstore_owners.py:478-490 inserts {role: 'webstore_owner'} into db.users, every later call to get_current_active_user() hydrates that doc into UserInDB and ValidationError → 500. Reproduction: POST /api/owner-portal/signup with portal-invite token → success; then GET /api/owner-portal/me with returned JWT → 500. Mitigation (1-line fix): add `WEBSTORE_OWNER = 'webstore_owner'` to UserRole in /app/backend/models/enums.py. No data migration needed.
